findings.title: availability(of:) traps on arithmetic overflow when the declared sizes of missing entries sum past Int64.max
findings.requirements: R-MAN-2 (untrusted manifest never crashes), R-MAN-3 (never crashes), R-STO-7 / R-SYN-10 (availability), R-NET-7 configuration maxAssetBytes = Int64.max ('unlimited', ArithmeticSafetyTests)
findings.problem: `report.bytesMissing += entry.byteSize ?? 0` is a plain, trapping Int64 addition over byte sizes the manifest declares. Every other figure built from manifest sizes saturates (PlanBuilder.adding, InFlightBytes, addingSaturating in 26 places, SizeGuard, PackProgressScaler), and the transport explicitly supports `maxAssetBytes = Int64.max` meaning 'unlimited' (Tests/ZTronAssetTransportTests/ArithmeticSafetyTests.swift:100, extremeConfiguredCaps). With that public configuration (AssetClientConfiguration.limits), a manifest whose missing entries declare sizes summing past Int64.max (two entries of 2^62 bytes are enough) crashes the process on the first availability(scope:) or ensureAvailable(scope:) call. The path is AssetClient.availability (AssetClient.swift:210) → SyncEngine.performAvailability → store.availability, and EngineCommands.swift:601/705 for ensureAvailable. The default limits cannot overflow, because 100,000 × 4 GiB is below Int64.max. The crash needs maxAssetBytes × maxEntries > Int64.max, so it is reachable only under a non-default but documented and tested configuration.
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/security/S3-SECU-01.swift (probe) and S3-SECU-01.txt (run output). The test process exited with 'unexpected signal code 5'. The crash report triggered thread shows: 'Swift runtime failure: arithmetic overflow' → 'AssetStore.currentAvailability(of:) AssetStore+Reads.swift 85' → 'AssetStore.availability(of:) AssetStore.swift 99' → 'S3SecurityStorageProbeTests.availabilitySaturatesBytesMissing() S3SecurityStorageProbeTests.swift 29' (EXC_BREAKPOINT / SIGTRAP). The manifest went through the real ManifestDecoder with ManifestLimits(maxAssetBytes: .max), was accepted (2 entries, 0 quarantined) and was applied by the store before the trap.
findings.repro: Copy S3-SECU-01.swift to Tests/ZTronAssetStorageTests/Core/S3SecurityStorageProbeTests.swift, then: swift test --scratch-path <scratch> --skip Benchmarks --filter S3SecurityStorageProbeTests
findings.fix: Saturate both additions: `report.bytesMissing = report.bytesMissing.addingSaturating(max(0, entry.byteSize ?? 0))` (the store's existing Int64.addingSaturating in Eviction/EvictionOrder.swift:381). Commit the probe as the regression test: it expects bytesMissing == Int64.max and missing == 2.

findings.title: The decoder accepts remote paths that the transport refuses on every fetch (empty segment, '.' segment, backslash, trailing slash)
findings.requirements: R-MAN-2 (per-entry violations quarantine the entry with a diagnostic), R-MAN-1 (manifests behave as before), TR1-10, ADR draft A-4.7 / orchestrator decision 3, ADR draft D-6
findings.problem: RemoteURL.make (ADR draft D-6) rejects `rejected(.invalidURL)` for empty components, `.` (also `%2E`), `\`, `?` and `#`. Fix round 3 (orchestrator decision 3) made the Model quarantine `?` and `#` 'instead of failing every fetch in the transport (TR1-10)', but did not do the same for the other spellings. The decoder still accepts `media//a.png`, `media/./a.png`, `./a.png`, `media/%2E/a.png`, `media\a.png` and `media/`. Such an entry is applied and planned, then fails at once on every attempt. ARCHITECTURE §7.6 maps `rejected(violation)` to `failed(.nextRun)` and answers waiters `.serverUnavailable(retryAfter: nil)`. So the entry is retried every run and misreported as a server problem instead of being quarantined with a diagnostic. The prior art fetched `a//b.png` with appendingPathComponent, so a manifest that relies on it decodes but no longer behaves as before. This is not a traversal: no such path can leave the base. It is a robustness and consistency gap that the recorded decision did not cover.
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/security/S3-SECU-02.swift and S3-SECU-02-03.log. Failing lines: '✘ Test "R-MAN-2: a remote path the transport refuses on every fetch is quarantined by the decoder" with 6 test cases failed after 0.001 seconds with 12 issues.' For the argument "media//a.png": 'Expectation failed: manifest.entries.map(\.identifier) == ["ok"] … media//a.png was accepted although no fetch of it can ever be made … → [ok, x]' and 'manifest.quarantinedCount → 0'. The transport side is already proven by the passing ForegroundBackendTests.invalidPaths ('R-NET-4: a remote path that could leave the base path is refused as an invalid URL', arguments "a//b", "a\\b", "a/%2E/b"; 151/151 transport tests passed, also under TSan). For "./a.png" and "media/", RemoteURL.make returns nil on the decoded "." and on the empty last component (RequestFactory.swift:74-80).
findings.repro: Copy S3-SECU-02.swift to Tests/ZTronAssetModelTests/Manifest/S3SecurityModelProbeTests.swift, then: swift test --scratch-path <scratch> --skip Benchmarks --filter S3SecurityModelProbeTests
findings.fix: Add one RemotePathViolation (for example `.emptyOrDotSegment` plus `.backslash`, or extend `.parentSegment`'s pass) so that the decoder quarantines exactly what RemoteURL.make refuses: an empty segment, a `.` segment (also `%2e`), and a `\`. Keep `%3F` allowed, as in A-4.7. Alternatively relax RemoteURL.make to the Model's rules and record the choice in an ADR. Either way, add a test that every path the decoder accepts yields a URL from RemoteURL.make.

findings.title: StagingFileName(parsing:) accepts non-canonical names, so a parsed name's rawValue names a different file
findings.requirements: R-SEC-2 (names under the root), R-CLN-3 (anything under staging/ that does not parse is foreign and collected), ADR-013
findings.problem: TransferAttempt(token:) accepts leading zeros (`01-2`, `1-02`) and TransferID(rawValue:) accepts any `c-[a-z0-9-]*`, not only `c-<64 hex>`. So StagingFileName(parsing:) is not 'nil for anything that is not exactly one of our names' (its own doc). A foreign `c-<h>.01-2.part` parses as ours, and its rawValue is `c-<h>.1-2.part`, which is a different file. StagingCollection.garbage then applies age rules instead of 'foreign: always removed'. listStaging (AssetStore+Reads.swift:172) keys the inventory by the parsed name, so two directory entries collapse onto one key, and stagingURL(name) addresses the canonical file, not the listed one. BackgroundTaskTag(decoding:) inherits the same leniency. Only a file planted inside the app's container can reach this, and no data is lost: age-based GC removes it eventually. Robustness only.
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/security/S3-SECU-03.swift (same probe file as -02) and S3-SECU-02-03.log. The run shows '✘ Test "R-SEC-2: staging names parse only in the canonical spelling the module writes" recorded an issue with 1 argument fileName → "c-aaaa…aaaa.1-02.part" … ↳ c-aaaa…aaaa.1-02.part parsed as c-aaaa…aaaa.1-2.part', and the same for ".01-2.part".
findings.repro: swift test --scratch-path <scratch> --skip Benchmarks --filter S3SecurityModelProbeTests
findings.fix: In StagingFileName(parsing:), require `parsed.rawValue == fileName`, or make TransferAttempt(token:) reject leading zeros. Make TransferID(rawValue:) require exactly 64 lowercase hex digits after `c-`/`l-` (ContentHash(hex:)). Commit the probe as the regression test.

security.searched:
Searched the transport, manifest, store, legacy-migration and Apple-tier surfaces, and found nothing beyond the three findings.

**App key and redirects (R-NET-4, R-SEC-1)**
- RedirectPolicy and Origin: hop cap, scheme, allow-list, key stripping that never returns; userinfo, trailing dots and percent-encoded hosts.
- Hop counter held as a URLProtocol property.
- Background path: the final origin is compared with the original after the fact; the key reaches a background request only with keyRedirectExposure == .acceptedByOwner, and routesToBackground agrees.
- httpAdditionalHeaders is empty on both sessions; ephemeral session with no cache, no cookies and no credential storage.
- AppKey redacts itself in description, debugDescription, Mirror and dump, and is not Codable.
- DiagnosticReportBuilder strips userinfo, query and fragment, and reports appKey as "<redacted>".
- Every log line is privacy .public, but identifiers are hashed, and engine record() logs only the class and a hash.
- ResponseFacts copies values only.
- BackgroundTaskTag carries no secret.
- Existing canary tests (Model, Transport loopback, Kit) genuinely send and scan the key.

**Size caps (R-NET-7)**
- SizeGuard saturates.
- announcedTotal is nil under any non-identity Content-Encoding.
- A 206's offset plus length saturates.
- Error bodies stop at a 64 KiB evidence cap.
- Staged size is compared with byteSize, with truncated vs sizeMismatch distinguished.
- Background expectedBytes must be within the cap.
- PackProgressScaler uses 128-bit arithmetic.
- MonotonicInstant.adding and Backoff clamp.

**Header parsing**
- Retry-After: at most 10 digits, UInt32, all three HTTP-date formats; dates are validated with no traps.
- Content-Range: at most 19 digits.
- ETag and Last-Modified: printable ASCII, at most 256 bytes.

**Manifest parser**
- Escaped keys and values, surrogates, UTF-8 validation, depth.
- Duplicates are detected on decoded bytes, and AssetID compares byte-wise, so canonical-equivalence collisions cannot occur.
- integralValue handles exponents and saturation.
- The `..` rule covers %2e, %2F, %5C, `\`, `?` and `#`.

**Store, legacy migration and Apple tier (R-SEC-2)**
- StoreLayout builds only from validated names; AssetFileExtension; blob-name parse.
- Publish takes an lstat size and compares it with the hashed size, so a planted link is rejected.
- Legacy planner component rules; non-following listings; phase 4 removes only listed items, and unlinks links without following them.
- The test-only CDNLocalStore.localURL confines paths.
- PackID and PackLocation reject a combining mark that hides a dot segment; LiveAssetPackBackend passes paths only to FilePath.
- The engine's byte sums saturate everywhere except S3-SECU-01.

**Test runs**
- Commands: `swift test --filter <Target>Tests` at load averages of 35 to 300.
- ZTronAssetTransportTests: 151 passed.
- ZTronAssetModelTests: 84 passed in 187.9 s, at a load of about 56.
- ZTronAssetAppleHostedTests: 104 passed.
- ZTronAssetTransportTests under TSan (`--sanitize=thread`): 151 passed in 4.9 s, no ThreadSanitizer warnings, load about 104 to 164.
- No flakes observed.
security.status:
I found 1 blocking issue and 2 non-blocking ones, each backed by a probe that was run. All work happened in a detached worktree at s3-base, which has been removed; the repository checkout's git status is unchanged.

**S3-SECU-01 (blocking, WP-B): crash on hostile manifest input.**
- What it does: AssetStore.availability(of:) adds up the declared byteSize of missing entries with a plain `+=`. Every other sum of manifest sizes in the code saturates instead.
- When it triggers: the documented and tested `maxAssetBytes = Int64.max` ("unlimited") configuration. A manifest declaring two missing entries of 2^62 bytes then traps the process on the first availability(scope:) or ensureAvailable(scope:) call.
- Evidence: the probe crashed with SIGTRAP, "Swift runtime failure: arithmetic overflow" at AssetStore+Reads.swift:85. The manifest was decoded and applied first, through the real ManifestDecoder.
- Limit: default limits cannot reach the overflow.
- Fix: one line per site, using the existing addingSaturating.

**S3-SECU-02 (non-blocking, WP-A): decoder and transport disagree on remote paths.**
- What it does: the decoder accepts remote paths with an empty or `.` segment, a backslash, or a trailing slash. The transport refuses each of these on every fetch with `rejected(.invalidURL)`.
- Consequence: such an entry is retried every run and reported to waiters as a server problem, instead of being quarantined with a diagnostic.
- Context: fix round 3 already applied exactly this reasoning to `?` and `#`, but not to these spellings.
- Evidence: 6 of 6 probe cases failed, with each entry accepted and 0 quarantined.

**S3-SECU-03 (non-blocking, WP-A): staging names parse in spellings the module never writes.**
- What it does: `StagingFileName(parsing:)` accepts non-canonical names, such as leading zeros in the attempt token or a `c-` prefix not followed by a hash.
- Consequence: a foreign file like `c-<h>.01-2.part` parses as ours, and its rawValue names a different file.
- Reach: only a file planted inside the app's container can trigger it.

**Not verified:**
- Nothing ran on the iOS Simulator.
- Only the transport tests ran under TSan.
- verify.sh was not run, so there is no VERIFY line to quote.

findings.title: Background transfer priority changes are not ordered: an older promotion lands after a newer demotion (D-9 reentrancy), so the OS task keeps the wrong priority
findings.requirements: R-NET-10 (MUST), H-4, H-5, C3 (REENTRANCY row D-9)
findings.problem: `BackgroundTransferCoordinator.setPriority` checks the attach token, then awaits `driver.snapshot()`, then writes `priorities[name]` and awaits `driver.setPriority`. After the listing, D-9 re-checks the token and whether the task is still live. It never checks that this request is still the newest one for the name. Two overlapping changes from the engine therefore land in whatever order their listings finish. Example: a promotion when a user waiter joins a bulk background job, then a demotion when the waiter withdraws. The OS task and `liveTransfers()` end at 0.75 while the engine's lane is bulk (0.25), and they stay there until another change arrives. On top of that, `BackgroundTransferHandle` sends every control (setPriority, pause, cancel) through its own unstructured `Task`, so even their arrival order at the actor is not guaranteed. The engine-level R-NET-10 test cannot catch either problem: it runs over FakeRemoteSource, whose handle records synchronously. Scope: only when the app turns the background route on (ADR-026; bulk only, off by default).
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/concurrency/S3-CONC-01.swift (test newestPriorityChangeWins), S3-CONC-01.log: `Expectation failed: changes.last == 0.25 ↳ the newest request was bulk (0.25), the OS task ends at Optional(0.75); changes [0.25, 0.75]` and `Expectation failed: await coordinator.liveTransfers().map(\.priority) == [0.25]` (run 09:06, load avg 48.6)
findings.repro: git worktree add --detach <wt> s3-base; cp .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/concurrency/S3-CONC-01.swift <wt>/Tests/ZTronAssetTransportTests/S3ConcurrencyProbeTests.swift; cd <wt>; swift test --scratch-path /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronAssetKit/.build-s3-concurrency --skip Benchmarks --filter 'ZTronAssetTransportTests.S3ConcurrencyProbeTests/newestPriorityChangeWins'
findings.fix: Make the newest request win inside the actor. Before the first await, bump a per-name request serial (`prioritySerial[name] += 1; let mine = ...`). After the listing, return unless `prioritySerial[name] == mine`, alongside the existing token and processed checks. Clear the serial in `process(.finished)`. Then deliver the handle's controls in order: feed them into one `AsyncStream` continuation per handle, drained by one task in FIFO order, instead of one `Task` per call. Without that, `setPriority(a); setPriority(b)` can still arrive as b then a. Add the probe as a regression test and amend ledger row D-9 to name the newest-request check.

findings.title: BackgroundEventsRelay.accept overwrites a pending completion handler: the first one is never called and the second is called before its own events are staged
findings.requirements: R-NET-3 (SHOULD), REENTRANCY row RE-S42 ('the relay's completion runs once, after the events that preceded it were staged')
findings.problem: `handlers[identifier] = completionHandler` replaces a handler that has not been completed yet. Sequence: UIKit hands a second handler for the same session while the facade's first `handleBackgroundEvents` task is still waiting. The first task's `relay.complete(identifier)` then calls the second handler, which is early because its own events are not yet staged. The second task finds no handler. The first handler UIKit handed over is never called, although Apple requires every one to be called.
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/concurrency/S3-CONC-02.swift (test secondHandlerKeepsFirst), S3-CONC-02.log: `Expectation failed: calls.sorted() == ["first", "second"] ↳ each handler UIKit handed over runs once: ["second"]` (run 09:06, load avg 48.6)
findings.repro: cp .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/concurrency/S3-CONC-02.swift <wt>/Tests/ZTronAssetTransportTests/S3ConcurrencyProbeTests.swift; swift test --scratch-path /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronAssetKit/.build-s3-concurrency --skip Benchmarks --filter 'ZTronAssetTransportTests.S3ConcurrencyProbeTests/secondHandlerKeepsFirst'
findings.fix: Keep every accepted handler: `handlers: [String: [(ticket: UInt64, handler: () -> Void)]]`. `accept` returns or records a ticket. `complete(identifier:ticket:)` calls and removes the handlers accepted up to that ticket, since their preceding events were staged when the wait that began after them returned. Calling all pending handlers is also acceptable, because the latest wait covers the earlier ones. Never drop one uncalled. Update RE-S42's wording and keep the probe as a test.

findings.title: A lagging subscriber gets run N+1's syncProgress before run N's syncFinished and before run N+1's syncStarted (stale .run progress slot reused in place)
findings.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/SubscriberQueue.swift:117-123 (progress slot replaced in place, keeps its first position); Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineEvents.swift:79-91 (retireProgress retires only .transfer slots from subscriber queues)
findings.requirements: R-SYN-12, H-9, ADR-023; SubscriberQueue's own documented contract ('Delivery order is the publication order of each slot's latest occurrence')
findings.problem: A progress slot that is still undelivered is replaced in place and keeps the queue position of its first occurrence. At run end, `retireProgress(.run)` clears only the trailing emission. It does not retire the undelivered `.run` slot from subscriber queues, unlike transfer keys, which retire with their transfer. So for a subscriber that has not read run 1's progress, run 2's first `syncProgress` lands in that old slot, ahead of `syncFinished(run1)` and `syncStarted(run2)`. A UI that hides its bar on syncFinished or resets it on syncStarted shows run 2's progress, then hides or resets it, and gets no later progress if none follows. No event is lost and the bound holds. Only the order is wrong, and it contradicts the queue's documented delivery order.
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/concurrency/S3-CONC-03.swift, S3-CONC-03.log. Engine level, test engineDeliversStartBeforeProgress: `Expectation failed: started < progress ↳ run 2's syncProgress at 3 precedes its syncStarted at 4: ["client", "conditions", "snapshot", "run", "runStarted", "runFinished", "clientEnd"]`. Unit level, test queueDeliversStartBeforeProgress: delivered `[syncProgress(run-2), syncFinished(run-1), syncStarted(run-2)]` (run 09:10, load avg 309)
findings.repro: cp .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/concurrency/S3-CONC-03.swift <wt>/Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/S3ConcurrencyProbeTests.swift; swift test --scratch-path /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronAssetKit/.build-s3-concurrency --skip Benchmarks --filter 'ZTronAssetSyncTests.S3EngineEventProbeTests'
findings.fix: Retire the run's progress key with its run, as a transfer's is. In `retireProgress(.run)`, call `subscribers[key]?.retire(.run)` for every subscriber, since `syncFinished` supersedes the undelivered progress. Then run 2's progress gets a fresh slot behind `syncStarted(run2)`. Alternatively, move a replaced progress slot to the tail, as the struct's doc says; that also changes the existing `subscriberQueueOrder` expectation, which is not a CDN test. Either way, make the SubscriberQueue doc match the behaviour and keep both probes.

findings.title: An asset that failed offline before the engine's first conditions reading is never retried when that reading shows a satisfied path (first reading is never an edge)
findings.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineConditions.swift:97 (`edge = satisfied && (previous.map {…} ?? false)`); Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineDispatch.swift:475 (user lane dispatched while `state.conditions == nil`); Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineFailures.swift:84-90 (offline → failed(.whenOnline) unless an edge passed during the attempt)
findings.requirements: R-SYN-13 (MUST), R-SYN-14 (watcher torn down at idle sets conditions to nil), H-5
findings.problem: An idle engine has no watcher and no conditions, because `reconcileIdle` sets `state.conditions = nil`. When work arrives, the watcher is spawned. User-initiated jobs are dispatched before it delivers its first reading, while other lanes wait for one. If that attempt fails `.offline` before the first reading arrives, `edgePassed` is false and the job becomes `failed(.whenOnline)`. Fail-fast answers the waiter `.offline`, but any other interest keeps the job: a prefetch group, a run claim or `ensureAvailable`. The first reading then reports a satisfied path. `apply` treats a first reading (`previous == nil`) as never an edge, so nothing re-queues the job. It waits for a second network edge that a steady network never sends, with no timer and no polling, until a user request or a later run revives it. Real-world window: a -1009 failure, then the network is back before NWPathMonitor's first callback. The window is narrow, but the stuck state is permanent.
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/concurrency/S3-CONC-04.swift (suite S3OfflineRetryProbeTests, GatedConditionsSource holds the post-idle observation), S3-CONC-04.log: `Expectation failed: after != .failed(.whenOnline) ↳ the path is satisfied, yet the asset waits for another edge: Optional(JobState.failed(RetryDisposition.whenOnline))` and `↳ a retry was started or queued: starts 1, state Optional(...failed(...whenOnline))`. The earlier expectations of the probe all passed (waiter answered `.offline`; job `failed(.whenOnline)` held by the group). Run 09:13, load avg 174.
findings.repro: cp .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/concurrency/S3-CONC-04.swift <wt>/Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/S3ConcurrencyProbeTests.swift; swift test --scratch-path /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronAssetKit/.build-s3-concurrency --skip Benchmarks --filter 'ZTronAssetSyncTests.S3OfflineRetryProbeTests'
findings.fix: Count a satisfied first reading as an edge for work that failed offline while no reading existed. Option 1: in `apply`, use `previous.map { … } ?? true` for the edge, so `owedOnEdge` jobs re-queue and `networkEdgeSerial` advances. It is a no-op when nothing failed, and a pending run waiting for an edge keeps the watcher alive. Option 2: in the `.offline` branch, when `state.conditions == nil`, mark the job owed on the first satisfied reading. Keep the probe as the regression test, and record the choice next to PROBE-C9C-3's rule in ARCHITECTURE §7.6.

concurrency.status:
I found 4 proven findings; 2 are blocking under the owner's bar.
- S3-CONC-01 (blocking): a background-transfer priority change can land after a newer one. The OS task then keeps 0.75 while the engine's lane is bulk, which breaks R-NET-10. It only matters when the app turns on the opt-in background route.
- S3-CONC-04 (blocking): an asset that fails offline before the engine's first conditions reading is never retried when that reading shows a satisfied path. This breaks R-SYN-13; the real-world window is narrow but the stuck state is permanent.
- S3-CONC-02 (not blocking): BackgroundEventsRelay drops a pending UIKit completion handler uncalled (R-NET-3 is a SHOULD).
- S3-CONC-03 (not blocking): a lagging subscriber receives run N+1's syncProgress before run N's syncFinished and run N+1's syncStarted. This contradicts SubscriberQueue's documented delivery order; no event is lost.

findings.title: phaseFourStopsListing (the known L5K-R27 (2) TSan flake): its poll reads listings() before heldUnits, so one round can release a second phase-4 listing unit and the oracle sees listings() → 3; root cause proven, fix (a) verified
findings.requirements: SPEC 7.1 Q-5 (zero flakes over full_run_repeats), Q-3 (suite clean under TSan), 7.2; R-STO-11 test integrity (CLAUDE.md G4)
findings.problem: The poll's condition `listings()` is a synchronous read of the fake volume's log: it copies the log, then filters every operation through `standardizedFileURL`, which is slow under TSan. The held-unit read comes after it, as a separate hop to the SteppedBlockingExecutor actor. Losing timeline, checked against SteppedBlockingExecutor.swift:30-46 and :60-62. (1) Round k: listings()==0, heldUnits.first==R (phase 4's root listing), release(R). release only resumes R's gate; R's work() runs later on the executor actor. (2) Round k+1 reads listings()==0, because R has not run yet. (3) R runs and records the root listing; the store resumes and submits phase 4's next listing U2, which is held. (4) Round k+1 then reads heldUnits==[U2] and releases it, so U2's listing runs. (5) Round k+2 sees listings()==2>0 and returns. requireHeldUnits(atLeast:1) now holds U3. (6) The stop (cancel or close) plus releaseAll runs U3, so listings()==3 and the `#expect(listings() == 2)` at :446 fails. The product is correct: in the replay, exactly one listing (the unit in flight) runs after the stop (`listings() == atStop + 1` holds). Only the test's oracle depends on the schedule. This reproduces the cycle-5 verifier's diagnosis in ADR-055 / L5K-R27 (2).
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/stability/S3-STAB-01-evidence.txt, S3-STAB-01.swift (deterministic replay), S3-STAB-01-fix-a.diff, runs-and-loads.txt. Its product-property line (:83, `listings() == atStop + 1`) passes. In the four full runs and the two TSan runs this test passed: 6 launches, 12 case runs.

findings.location: Tests/ZTronAssetStorageTests/Cleanup/EvictionTests.swift:64-72, :118-126, :235-243, :553-561, :615-623; EvictionOverlapTests.swift:103-111; IdempotencyTests.swift:140-148; GarbageCollectionTests.swift:308-316 (cancelDuringSecondRemoval, used at :372), :588-596 (also :516-524, where the extra release only changes which interleaving noPhantomDoom covers)
findings.requirements: SPEC 7.1 Q-5, Q-3, 7.2; tests of R-CLN-2, R-CLN-4, R-CLN-12 (CLAUDE.md G4: their oracles hold only under one schedule)
findings.problem: Each poll evaluates `if <condition> { return … }; if let unit = await executor.heldUnits.first { release(unit) }`. The condition is a synchronous read of the fake volume, or a hop to the store actor through `harness.record`/`state`. A round whose condition read predates the run of the unit released by the previous round, and whose `heldUnits` read follows that unit's run and the store's submission of its next unit, releases that next unit. That is the S3-STAB-01 timeline with a different condition. The unit released is the one the test means to hold. In chunkYieldRevalidates it is eviction's between-chunk yield, so y2 and y3 are evicted before the test reads y2 and leases y3. In chunkCountsRecords and in the tests at :553/:615 it is again the chunk yield, so firstChunk includes a second chunk. In evictionDuringReusingPublication it is the placement unit, so the publication ends and `requireHeldUnits` then waits out the time limit. In EvictionOverlapTests it is the first-chunk yield, so the plan no longer lists o2 and o3. In cancelledCollection(.stagingGC) it is the second removal: the third removal is submitted before the cancel, the collection removes all three files and returns success. In cancelDuringSecondRemoval it is the second removal unit, so `exists(second)` fails. In sweepChunksReleaseActor it is the sweep's chunk yield, so planted[1] is doomed. PurgeTests.untilPurgeReturnsOrWaits (:376-391) already reads `heldUnits` before its condition, which closes the window.
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/stability/S3-STAB-02.swift (deterministic replays of three representative sites; each waits where the poll races, then runs the original oracle unchanged) and S3-STAB-02-evidence.txt. Observed rate on the unchanged originals: 0 issues in 200 TSan repetitions of each of the 22 tests in these suites, at load ~75-80. Their conditions are cheap reads or store-actor hops, so the read-to-hop window is far narrower than phaseFourStopsListing's whole-log filter. findings.title: Fallback chain's network step downloads an asset of the wrong kind at userInitiated before rejecting it; the prior art rejected it without a request
findings.requirements: R-CAR-2 ('identical observable behaviour'), SPEC 7.3 'Facade parity'
findings.problem: The prior art's network step, ZTronCarouselCore CDNAssetResolver.swift:46, checks `candidateExtensions.contains(asset.fileExtension)` against the cached manifest entry and returns nil before any download. `AssetFallbackChain.fetch` instead calls `client.resolve(id, priority: .userInitiated)` first and checks `url.pathExtension` afterwards. So `fetch("clip", kind: .image)` on a catalog entry that is an .mp4 downloads the whole video at top priority, preempting prefetch, stores it, and only then throws notFound. The existing test (FallbackChainTests.swift:151) uses an asset already held, so it cannot see the download. The compatibility shim copies the same order, and its doc comment cites ADR-037. ADR-037 records only three deviations: lookup after start, the extension filter at the local step, and the bundle index. It does not record downloading before the candidate check. The impact is small (a mismatched catalog entry), but the deviation is unrecorded and observable.

findings.title: interactiveConcurrencyAtCritical (ADR-036) is untested, and user work dispatched before the first conditions element after idle is never held to it
findings.requirements: R-SYN-7 (thermal state), ADR-036, ARCHITECTURE §12 sync-2 S2-29 ('interactiveConcurrencyAtCritical enforced'), CLAUDE.md G4
findings.problem: There are two parts. (a) The cap path, EngineDispatch.swift:79, has 0 executions in the suite. A mutant returning maxConcurrentTransfers survives every Sync, Kit and compatibility test. (b) The real defect: when the engine goes idle, the watcher stops and the conditions are set to nil (R-SYN-14). The next user-initiated burst is dispatched optimistically with no thermal cap, by design in sync.md §11.1. When the first element then reports .critical, apply() never trims the extra running user transfers. ADR-036 promises 'one user-initiated transfer at .critical', and S2-29 is recorded as enforced, but neither record considered this window. It is not a SPEC MUST (R-SYN-7's thermal clause binds bulk work), so it is non-blocking.
findings.evidence: The mutant S3-CONF-04.mutant.diff survives the full Sync suite (351 tests), Kit (85) and compatibility (71). Probe (a) fails under it: 'S3ConformanceProbeTests.swift:130:9: Expectation failed: state.running == … interactiveConcurrencyAtCritical' (evidence-mutants-04-05.txt), and passes on s3-base. Probe (b) uses a gated conditions source and fails on s3-base, deterministically 5/5: 'S3ConformanceProbeTests.swift:170:9 ↳ running at .critical: 3 ↳ state.running → 3 ↳ harness.configuration.power.interactiveConcurrencyAtCritical → 1'. Before the source was gated, an ungated version of (b) depended on timing (it passed once inside the full Sync run), which is why the committed version gates it.
findings.repro: Copy S3-CONF-04.swift into Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/, then: swift test --scratch-path <scratch> --skip Benchmarks --filter S3ConformanceEngineProbeTests (fails on s3-base). With git apply S3-CONF-04.mutant.diff, test (a) fails as well.
findings.fix: In apply(_:), when thermal reaches .critical, preempt or pause the running user-initiated transfers beyond max(1, interactiveConcurrencyAtCritical), as preemptForUser does, and re-queue them. Alternatively, record the optimistic window in ADR-036 and amend S2-29. Then commit both probes.

findings.title: Engine shutdown holds the engine's actor for 17-22 ms at the 10,000 reference scale (C2), including the mid-session rootVanished reopen
findings.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineLifecycle.swift:470 (performShutdown; job-table sorts at :493 and :580; resumeEverything :516-602); reached mid-session from Sources/ZTronAssetKit/Facade/ClientLifecycle.swift:206
findings.requirements: CLAUDE.md C2; SPEC 4.2 (cooperative pool <= ~10 ms at a stretch); SPEC 6 reference N = 10,000; R-SYN-15; P-9 (heartbeat context)
findings.problem: performShutdown's first turn does all the teardown synchronously. It sorts the whole 10,000-entry job table twice (66-character TransferID strings) only to cancel handles, although only in-flight jobs have one. It resumes every waiter continuation (10,000) and every group, then drops the job table and every parked index, which deallocates 10,000 Job values. All of this happens in one actor turn on a cooperative-pool thread. With only the 10,000-member group (no waiters) the turn is still 10.6-13.5 ms. The same path runs while the app is live, when ClientLifecycle.performReopen retires the old engine after a rootVanished. R-SYN-4's handle release had the same one-turn shape and was already fixed (15 ms down to 4 ms); shutdown was not.

Release run, load 14.5: 'C2 shutdown under 10,000 prefetch members and 10,000 waiting resolves: longest actor wait 17.6755 ms ... runs [17.6755, 17.01125, 20.275375]; at 1,000: 1.255584 ms ...; the 10,000-member group without waiters: 12.767625 ms'. With production DispatchBlockingExecutors (dispatchBench) the best run was 18.957 ms. Other release runs: best 18.73, 19.66 and 21.24 ms. Debug: best 51.1 ms.
findings.repro: git worktree add --detach <wt> s3-base; cp S3-PERF-01-S3PerfShutdownProbe.swift <wt>/Tests/ZTronAssetKitBenchmarks/S3PerfShutdownProbe.swift; cd <wt>; swift test -c release -Xswiftc -enable-testing --scratch-path <scratch> --filter 'shutdownTurns|handleReleaseTurns'
findings.fix:
Bound the teardown per turn:
1. Cancel handles over state.inFlight (or the active jobs) instead of sorting all jobs, twice.
2. Move the drained continuation tables out of state and resume them in bounded batches (for example 512, as readmissionsPerTurn does) in owned follow-up turns while lifecycle == .shuttingDown. CheckedContinuation is Sendable, so an owned task off the actor can resume them in chunks.
3. Hand the retired job table and parked sets to that task, so they are deallocated off the actor.
Commit the probe as a SyncBenchmarks C2 benchmark next to handleReleaseTurns.

findings.requirements: P-13 batch_ms_max (owner item ADR-050); SPEC 6 'propose a new number'
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/performance/S3-PERF-03-P13UnlinkProbe-main.swift (swiftc -O). Clean run S3-PERF-03-unlink-probe-run6.txt, load 12.9: '[load 12.9] ... M1-matrix-fresh-fanout-default: unlink ... max 4.43 ms, >2ms 10, >4ms 7 | spin(45us cpu) ... max 0.06 ms, >2ms 0 ... | unlink-stall indices ... first [64, 920, 1831, 2645, 3528, 3538, 4416, 4418, 5743, 5746]'. M5 flat settled: '>2ms 12 ... spin >2ms 0 ... first [511, 1055, 1605, 2146, 2662, 3214, 3755, 4301, 4302, 4932]'. M7 .noindex settled: '>2ms 11'. M8 utility fresh: '>2ms 11, max 6.62'. findings.fix:
No code change removes the stall. It sits inside one unlink(2) and recurs by count, so smaller units, rate limiting, pre-syncing blobs and fan-out changes do not avoid it. Raising the deletion queue's QoS only removes the preemption share under load, at an energy cost for background GC. Options for the owner:
(B, robust) Raise batch_ms_max to about 15 ms. One stall (up to about 11 ms in ADR-050's quiet runs, 6.6 ms here) plus the 1 ms unit budget fits.
(A, marginal) Judge the per-batch bound on a percentile. At about 1 stall per 900 unlinks and about 20 unlinks per unit, 1.5-2 % of units contain one, so p99 passes only when fewer than half of the stalls exceed the 4 ms headroom. p98 would be robust.
(C) Judge the batch bound on what it protects. Units run on the dedicated metadata DispatchQueue, so a stalled unlink holds neither the store's actor nor a cooperative-pool thread. The bound would be the longest actor hold between units (as StorageBenchmarks.actorStretches measures) plus unit on-CPU time, with the wall-clock maximum printed as information.
All three are SPEC 6 or quality-gates decisions; nothing was edited (G1).

findings.title: The reaper's re-insertion of keys a unit did not attempt is O(remaining) per key, making the reclaim quadratic
findings.requirements: P-13 gc_total_s_max (met at 10,000; scaling); SPEC goal 4 (battery)
findings.problem: The queue is an ArraySlice. With 64-key batches and the 1 ms unit time budget (ADR draft B-10), a unit attempts about 20 keys. The about 44 keys it did not attempt are each put back with queue.insert near the front, which shifts the whole remaining queue every time. The reclaim's actor work is therefore O(n squared / unit size). At 10,000 blobs it is within P-13's 2.0 s total, but the total doubles roughly 3x per doubling of the set.
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/performance/S3-PERF-04-S3PerfReapProbe.swift (each unlink advances a ManualTimeSource by 50 us, so every unit stops after 20 unlinks, as on the reference volume), output in S3-PERF-04-output.txt. Release: 'S3-PERF reap scaling (wall seconds of runDueWork): [(key: 10000, value: 0.548809792), (key: 20000, value: 1.103597583), (key: 40000, value: 3.463065958)]; 40,000 / 20,000 = 3.137978925783856 (max 2.5)'. Failing line: 'S3PerfReapProbe.swift:30:9: Expectation failed: ratio <= ratioMax'. findings.repro: cp S3-PERF-04-S3PerfReapProbe.swift <wt>/Tests/ZTronAssetKitBenchmarks/; swift test -c release -Xswiftc -enable-testing --scratch-path <scratch> --filter reapScaling
findings.fix: Keep the sorted queue as an Array with a cursor. Build each batch from the cursor without consuming it, and after the unit advance the cursor by outcome.attempted only. The keys that were not attempted, put back to doomed, stay in place and are re-validated by the next batch's deletionBlocker check. This costs O(1) per key and keeps the order unchanged.

findings.title: Each user-initiated publication copies the whole present table on the store's actor, making ensureAvailable-style runs quadratic
findings.location: Sources/ZTronAssetStorage/Store/AssetStore+Snapshot.swift:15-21 (refreshPresentEntry) and :43-49 (installSnapshot shares presentTable as the snapshot's entries); Store/AssetStore+Publish.swift:172
findings.requirements: R-SYN-10 (ensureAvailable fetches at user-initiated priority); SPEC goal 4 (battery); no SPEC 6 budget, so non-blocking
findings.problem: A .userInitiated publication installs at once. The snapshot's entries is the store's presentTable, shared copy-on-write, and the sink (SnapshotMirror) keeps it. The next publication's refreshPresentEntry therefore copies the whole present table, retaining an id, a URL and an extension per entry, on the store's actor. A run of n user-initiated publications, such as ensureAvailable over a scope, costs O(n squared). Bulk and prefetch publications install at most every snapshotInstallInterval and do not pay this. The cause is inferred from the code; the probe proves the superlinear cost.
findings.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/performance/S3-PERF-05-S3PerfPublishProbe.swift, output in S3-PERF-05-output.txt. Release, load 12 rising: 'S3-PERF publish scaling: user-initiated [(key: 2500, value: 1.315904465), (key: 5000, value: 3.9373557310000002), (key: 10000, value: 10.667697384)] s (10,000 / 5,000 = 2.709355748582728); bulk [(key: 2500, value: 1.058472739), (key: 5000, value: 2.155753501), (key: 10000, value: 2.324882279)] s'. Failing line: 'S3PerfPublishProbe.swift:29:9: Expectation failed: userRatio <= ratioMax'.
findings.repro: cp S3-PERF-05-S3PerfPublishProbe.swift <wt>/Tests/ZTronAssetKitBenchmarks/; swift test -c release -Xswiftc -enable-testing --scratch-path <scratch> --filter userInitiatedPublicationScaling
findings.fix: Make a user-initiated install O(changes) instead of O(present). Give AssetSnapshot a shared, rarely rebuilt base table plus a small overlay of the entries changed since the base. Lookup reads the overlay first, which stays O(1). Rebuild the base off the hot path when the overlay passes about sqrt(n) entries. Alternatively, double-buffer the present table using ack.retired, which the store already receives back. Keep the 'installed before publish returns' contract.

verdicts.reason: I reproduced this at s3-base (b5796ba) in my own detached worktree, with load averages around 42. The hunter's probe, copied unchanged, crashed the test process with 'unexpected signal code 5'. The new crash report swiftpm-testing-helper-2026-10-29-094735.ips shows EXC_BREAKPOINT/SIGTRAP, 'Swift runtime failure: arithmetic overflow', and the stack AssetStore.currentAvailability(of:) AssetStore+Reads.swift:85 → AssetStore.availability(of:) AssetStore.swift:99 → the probe. Lines 70 and 85 both use a plain `report.bytesMissing += entry.byteSize ?? 0`. The probe is not broken. When I changed only those two additions to `addingSaturating(max(0, …))` (S3-SECU-01-fix.diff), it passed, so `missing == 2` and `bytesMissing == .max` hold. The crash is therefore only the overflow. The manifest goes through the real ManifestDecoder and its entries are valid under the configured limits. The input reaches this code through the public API. AssetClientConfiguration.limits is public and is never clamped (`clamped()` exists only for SyncTuning). EngineManifest.swift:193 decodes remote manifests with `self.configuration.limits`. AssetClient.availability (AssetClient.swift:210), SyncEngine.performAvailability (EngineCommands.swift:540) and the ensureAvailable paths (EngineCommands.swift:601 and :705) all call store.availability. Neither DECISIONS nor the ADR drafts restrict maxAssetBytes. The transport tests treat Int64.max as a supported 'unlimited' cap (ArithmeticSafetyTests.swift:100). Default limits cannot overflow, because 100,000 × 4 GiB is far below Int64.max. Any configured cap of about 92 TB or more lets a remote manifest within those limits crash the process. That is a crash caused by untrusted manifest content, which breaks the R-MAN-2 MUST 'treat the manifest as untrusted input … never crash' and meets the owner's 'crashes' bar. It is BLOCKING. The owner is WP-B: Store/AssetStore+Reads.swift is a WP-B Store/ file (ARCHITECTURE §1.1/§1.2). Evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/confirm-security/S3-SECU-01.swift, S3-SECU-01.txt and S3-SECU-01-fix.diff.

I reproduced this at s3-base. The hunter's model probe failed with 12 issues: all 6 paths were accepted (entries [ok, x], quarantinedCount 0). My own probe (S3-SECU-02.swift in the transport tests) decodes each path with ManifestDecoder and then calls the real internal RemoteURL.make. For media//a.png, media/./a.png, ./a.png, media/%2E/a.png, media\a.png and media/, it reports 'decoder accepted=true, RemoteURL.make=nil'. The control path media/ok.png passes. I checked the code. HTTPRemoteSource.transfer:182 returns `.failed(.rejected(.invalidURL))` when RemoteURL.make returns nil. EngineFailures.swift:192-194 maps `.rejected` to `failed(.nextRun)` and gives waiters `.serverUnavailable(retryAfter: nil)`. The breaker outcome is neutral. Nothing in Sync or Storage checks remotePath beforehand. So the entry is planned, fails at once on every run, and is misreported as a server problem. Why it is not blocking: the SPEC's R-MAN-2 remotePath violation list (relative, ≤1,024 bytes, no `..`, scheme, authority or control character) does not include these spellings, so the decoder meets the MUST. Draft A-4.7 explicitly says '`.` … stay allowed' in the Model. Draft D-6 records that the transport rejects empty, `.` and `\` components. There is no crash, no data loss and no traversal; only the Model/transport mismatch for these spellings went unhandled. This is a confirmed consistency/robustness gap and NON-blocking. The owner is WP-A (Sources/ZTronAssetModel/**). The alternative fix would touch WP-D's RequestFactory.swift. Evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/confirm-security/S3-SECU-02.swift, S3-SECU-02-03-model-probe.swift, S3-SECU-02-03.log and S3-SECU-02-03-confirm.log.

The only way to reach this is a file planted inside the app's own container, not a path derived from manifest text, so the R-SEC-2 MUST (no escape from the root) and I-4 still hold. security.status: I confirmed all three security findings independently at s3-base (b5796ba) in a detached worktree (.build-s3-confirm-security-wt) using scratch path .build-s3-confirm-security. One build of the tests took 68 s at load averages of about 27 to 45. Filtered probe runs took milliseconds each, at load averages of about 26 to 42. S3-SECU-01 is confirmed and BLOCKING (WP-B). The hunter's probe traps with 'arithmetic overflow' at AssetStore+Reads.swift:85, according to a crash report I generated myself. A two-line saturating fix makes the probe pass, which rules out a broken probe. The input reaches this code from a remote manifest under a public, unclamped configuration (limits.maxAssetBytes ≥ about 92 TB, which the transport treats as a supported 'unlimited' cap), and the result is a process crash. S3-SECU-02 is confirmed and NON-blocking (WP-A). For all six paths, the decoder accepts and RemoteURL.make rejects, and the engine then maps the failure to failed(.nextRun) and .serverUnavailable. This does not break the SPEC's R-MAN-2 list, and A-4.7 and D-6 record each side of the mismatch. S3-SECU-03 is confirmed and NON-blocking (WP-A). I also wrote a confirmation for the direction that matters for H-4 (confirm-concurrency/S3-CONC-01-reverse.swift). An older demotion lands after a newer promotion, so the OS task ends at 0.25 (changes [0.75, 0.75, 0.25]) while a user is waiting.

I checked whether the interleaving can happen outside the fake. The hold seam is the same `holdNextSnapshot(.afterListing)` that the existing BackgroundInterleavingTests use, and in production three points can reorder controls:
(1) `BackgroundTransferHandle.setPriority/pause/cancel` (BackgroundSupport.swift:700-719) start one nonisolated `Task` per call on the global executor, so they can reach the actor in either order.
(2) `setPriority` (:422-441) awaits `driver.snapshot()`. The live driver does a holder-actor hop and `session.allTasks` off the actor, so a later request can finish its listing first. D-9 re-checks the token and processed set, but never whether this request is still the newest.
(3) `LiveBackgroundSessionDriver.setPriority` (BackgroundSessionBackend.swift:79) runs another `allTasks` and then `task.priority =` outside the coordinator, so two writes race there too.

The engine calls `handle.setPriority(lane)` synchronously on every lane change (EngineJobs.swift:197, EngineDispatch.swift:637-642) and never re-applies it later. A wrong value therefore stays until the next lane change.

Recorded decisions do not cover this. D-10 (adr-drafts/d.md) records the unstructured task per control but only weighs shutdown cancellation, not ordering. ADR-021 chose synchronous controls precisely so that controls stay ordered (S1-06), and this handle defeats that. ARCHITECTURE §7.5 says the priority is a hint, but that concerns what the OS does with the value. Here the library itself leaves the task at the value of an older lane, which breaks R-NET-10's MUST that engine priority maps to the URLSession task priority.

Scope: the route is off by default (ADR-026) and only carries key-free bulk work, so today's production configuration does not reach it.

Not refuted: the engine-level R-NET-10 test is not a G4 violation. It verifies the engine's ordering over FakeRemoteSource, as documented, but it does not cover the background coordinator.

The proposed fix is sound: a per-name request serial checked after the listing, plus one FIFO control stream per handle. Owner is WP-D (Sources/ZTronAssetTransport/**).

Reproduced (09:53): calls == ["second"], so the first handler is never called. `BackgroundEventsRelay.accept` (BackgroundSupport.swift:733-750) assigns `handlers[identifier] = completionHandler` and overwrites an uncompleted handler. `complete` removes and calls whatever is stored.

The coordinator side makes the early call real. One `.backgroundEventsFinished` runs `resumeFinishWaiters()` (BackgroundSupport.swift:579-584) and wakes both facade tasks (AssetClient.swift:435-454). The first task's `relay.complete` then calls the second handler, and the second task finds nothing.

No recorded decision covers this. The existing relay test only checks one handler completed once, and a fix that calls every pending handler keeps that test passing without a public API change.

Non-blocking because I could not prove the trigger. R-NET-3 is a SHOULD, and nothing shows that UIKit hands a second handler for the same session identifier while the first is still pending. That is device-only behaviour and goes under Not verified. It is not a Swift continuation or task leak, and no data is lost.

Owner is WP-D, since the relay lives in Transport. WP-G is only involved if the ticket variant changes `AssetClient.handleBackgroundEvents`.

Both probes reproduced (09:53):

- Engine: run 2's syncProgress is at index 3 and its syncStarted at index 4.

Cause, checked in the code: `SubscriberQueue.publish` replaces an undelivered progress slot in place, so it keeps its first sequence. `retireProgress` (EngineEvents.swift:70-79) retires only `.transfer` slots from subscriber queues, never `.run`. Run 2's first progress therefore reuses run 1's old queue position.

Keeping position on in-place replacement is deliberate: EngineUnitTests `subscriberQueueOrder` pins it ('progress first: it kept its position'). The SubscriberQueue doc line ('publication order of each slot's latest occurrence') is inaccurate.

No recorded decision covers the run key. ADR-023 retires only transfer keys.

Non-blocking:
- The public AssetEvent contract promises publication order only for terminal events.
- R-SYN-12's MUST clauses all hold: newest-wins, the bound, and no terminal event dropped.
- No event is lost. The effect is a transient UI ordering glitch for a lagging subscriber.

Owner is WP-F.

Reproduced (09:53): the job stays `failed(.whenOnline)` with starts 1 after a satisfied first reading. I added two tests to rule out a timing artifact (confirm-concurrency/S3-CONC-04-confirm.swift, 09:58, load 17.5). Both pass, which confirms the defect state:
(a) The job stays failed with 1 start after the engine is quiescent (armedTimers 0, scheduledDeadlines 0, watcher kept) and after a further reading of the same network. Only a real down-then-up edge retries it (starts 2).
(b) Control: the same sequence with an unsatisfied first reading followed by a satisfied one is retried. The only difference is the first-reading rule `previous.map{…} ?? false` (EngineConditions.swift:91).

Code path checked:
- `gate` (EngineDispatch.swift:475) dispatches user work while `conditions == nil`.
- The `.offline` branch (EngineFailures.swift:84-90) sees no edge passed and marks the job failed.
- `hasWork` keeps the watcher alive for the held job, so nothing else re-queues it.

There is a recorded decision: L4-C10-12 ('the first conditions element is never an edge', Not changed, citing F-16/L4-R3). It does not cover this case. That verifier's own text (.build-orchestrator/l4-close10-remaining-f.json) considered only the order where the element is applied before the failure. It judged 'not a liveness defect for a waiter' and states 'I did not build a probe for a group member'.

This finding covers what that record left out: the failure comes before any reading, and a non-waiter interest (group, run claim, ensureAvailable) keeps the job until some later network change. Both precedents allow exactly one bounded retry in an ambiguous case:
- F-16 grants runs one debounced retry for 'its first element was not in yet'.
- PROBE-C9C-3 retries a job once when an edge passed during the attempt.
Jobs get zero retries in the nil-to-satisfied case. A one-shot retry is not polling, so R-SYN-13's MUST (retry when the path becomes satisfied) is broken in a case the record did not consider.

The real-world window is narrow: the device is offline at the attempt and the path comes back before NWPathMonitor's first callback. A user request revives the asset, and nothing hangs or is lost. Under the strict bar, though, proven plus a MUST break makes it blocking.

Owner is WP-F.
